Patients leave before noon with their medicines reconciled, and fewer come back within 30 days.

trace_links.n: Ready rooms and instruments: no avoidable cancelled surgery
trace_links.story: Every instrument tray is ready on time, so no surgery is cancelled for a missing instrument.
Three call centers become one access center. Labor is forecast over budget because schedulers overlap for six weeks.

Scan every tray at every step so a tray at risk is known the evening before.

A nurse call within 48 hours of discharge for every high-risk patient.

Interfaces to two more hospitals' admission systems.
Find the causes of denials by payer and service line and fix them upstream.
Quarterly scheduling and referral licenses. Matches the contract and the seat count.
Bills 60 overlap shifts; 14 have no sign-off from the access center. Hold until the shifts are confirmed.
Scanners received and installed in two of four hospitals, as the order says.

Monthly workspace subscription. Matches the order.

controls.t: Access to the clinical record is reviewed every quarter
Leavers lose access on their last day
Emergency access to a chart is reviewed within a day
Medication orders are verified by a pharmacist before dispensing
Controlled substance counts match at every shift change
Every sterilizer load has a biological indicator result
Trays are released only with a complete load record
Downtime procedures are tested twice a year
Backups of the clinical record are restored as a test each month
Claims edits run before every submission
Prior authorization is recorded before scheduled procedures
Supplier agreements cover patient data before access is granted
Patient identity is confirmed with two identifiers
Interface errors are worked within four hours
Changes to clinical systems go through the change board
Privileged accounts use a second factor
Device gateways get security patches each month
Safety event reports are reviewed by quality within three days
Charge changes have a second approver
Staff complete privacy training every year

audits.t: Two units missed controlled substance counts in August
